new_statements.quote: Les travaux effectués sur l'Akyé rendent compte de trois ou quatre tons ponctuels (Kutsch Lojenga & Elizabeth Hood, 1982; Adopo & Bogny 1994 ; Kouadio 1996). Il s'agit des tons Super Haut (SH), Haut (H), Moyen (M) et Bas (B). (Cf. (1)). Certaines de ces études ont, par ailleurs, montré que le ton super haut (désormais SH) est un ton H sous-jacent (Adopo & Bogny 1994).
new_statements.translation: The work done on Akyé reports three or four level tones (Kutsch Lojenga & Elizabeth Hood 1982; Adopo & Bogny 1994; Kouadio 1996). These are the Super-High (SH), High (H), Mid (M) and Low (B) tones (cf. (1)). Some of these studies have moreover shown that the super-high tone (henceforth SH) is an underlying H tone (Adopo & Bogny 1994).
new_statements.citation: Bogny Yapo, Joseph. 2013. Le ton super haut à l'interface morphosyntaxe-phonologie en akyé. Sudlangues 20: 94-112.
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Opened (19 pp., text layer, Sudlangues 20, pp. 94-112). The quoted passage is on p. 95 under '0. INTRODUCTION', first paragraph, word for word: 'Les travaux effectués sur l'Akyé rendent compte de trois ou quatre tons ponctuels (Kutsch Lojenga & Elizabeth Hood, 1982; Adopo & Bogny 1994; Kouadio 1996). Il s'agit des tons Super Haut (SH), Haut (H), Moyen (M) et Bas (B). (Cf. (1)). Certaines de ces études ont, par ailleurs, montré que le ton super haut (désormais SH) est un ton H sous-jacent (Adopo & Bogny 1994).' Example (1) on p. 95 gives the four-way minimal set nàe SH/H/M/B ('champ en jachère' / 'peigne' / 'beau-père' / 'fruit'); p. 97 section I lists the contour tones MB, BM, MH, SHM, SHB…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Attié/Akyé is a register-tone language with three phonological level tones (H, M, L) plus a derived super-high (upstepped H), and contour tones (MB, BM, MH, SHM, SHB); tones are lexical on nouns and verbs. No opened source says anything about word stress or accent — neither its position nor its absence — so no stress rule can be stated.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not mentioned in any opened source.
new_statements.exceptions: None (no stress description exists to have exceptions). Tone-wise: the super-high tone is not phonemic but arises from H + a floating/clitic non-H tone inside a prosodic domain (Bogny 2013).
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level tone; Bogny 2013 discusses prosodic domains / phonological words only for the H-to-SH upstep. Adopo 2008 (Revue du LTML 1, p. 2) independently gives the same inventory: 'un système tonal composé de tons ponctuels et de tons modulés.. deux (2) tons modulés : le ton très haut bas (THB) et le moyen bas (MB) et trois tons ponctuels (haut (H) bas (B) moyen (M))'. Variety: Bogny and Adopo work on Akyé generally (Bogny's earlier DEA was on the Lépin dialect of Grand-Alépé; Kouadio on Memni/Alépé); Méraud 1902 on Nindin (Memni).
new_statements.identity_note: Bogny 2013 and Adopo 2008 describe Akyé (= Attié, atti1239) in general, drawing on Kutsch Lojenga & Hood 1982 (Anyama dialect), Adopo & Bogny 1994/1996 and Kouadio 1996 (Memni/Alépé); Bogny's own earlier fieldwork was on the Lépin dialect of Grand-Alépé. Méraud 1902 describes the Nindin (Memni) variety. Ahoua & Brouh 2009 (not opened) describe Bodin. All are dialects of the single Glottolog languoid atti1239; no separate dialect glottocodes.
